turns.question: Which retention outcome should the product enforce for customer uploads once report work is complete?
What user-facing deletion semantics should apply given disaster-recovery backups retain deleted objects for 30 days?

contract.G: DECISION: Automatically remove old customer uploads on a defined schedule. FACT: Uploads may still be referenced by completed reports. DECISION: Keep report summaries after upload deletion.
contract.T: DECISION: Delete each upload 90 days after its last associated report finishes. DECISION: Preserve report summaries while removing upload objects. DECISION: Present deletion as final to users even though backup copies may persist temporarily.
contract.S: FACT: Backups retain deleted objects for 30 days. DECISION: This slice covers primary upload deletion timing, preservation of summaries, and user-facing semantics. ASSUMPTION: References from completed reports can rely on summaries without requiring original upload bytes after the 90-day window.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify uploads are deleted from primary storage 90 days after the last report finishes. DECISION: Verify report summaries remain accessible after upload deletion. DECISION: Verify user messaging states deletion is final. FACT: Backup copies may still age out within 30 days under disaster recovery.
contract.X: DECISION: Stop after defining the reversible retention rule, preserved artifacts, and deletion messaging. UNKNOWN: No accepted organization-wide retention policy exists yet.
contract.P: DECISION: Use the 90-day-after-last-report rule as an authorized reversible default until a formal retention policy is accepted. DECISION: Revisit if report access requires original uploads or policy changes.

turns.question: What exact privacy boundary must local-only processing enforce for file content, metadata, derived text, AI features, and telemetry?

contract.G: DECISION: Add local-only file processing with no customer file data leaving the device. FACT: A remote AI provider receives derived text today. FACT: An on-device parser supports the primary format.
contract.T: DECISION: Keep file bytes, file metadata, and derived text entirely on-device. DECISION: Do not send file-related content to remote AI services. DECISION: Do not include file-related content in telemetry, including error payload excerpts.
contract.S: DECISION: This slice covers primary-format local parsing, AI/privacy boundary enforcement, and telemetry suppression for file-related data. FACT: Telemetry can include error payload excerpts today. ASSUMPTION: The on-device parser is sufficient for the primary format in the first reversible slice.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify no outbound network path receives file bytes, metadata, or derived text during processing. DECISION: Verify telemetry contains no file-derived excerpts or metadata in success and error cases. DECISION: Verify primary-format files can be processed fully on-device.
contract.X: DECISION: Stop after the local-only privacy boundary and first-slice verification are defined. UNKNOWN: Non-primary formats are not committed in this slice.
contract.P: DECISION: Treat strict on-device handling for content, metadata, derived text, AI, and telemetry as the reversible default. DECISION: Reassess only if a later explicit exception is approved.

turns.question: What refund authority should support agents have without owner involvement, including any limit and required justification?
Within that authority, should support agents be allowed to issue partial refunds as well as full refunds?

contract.G: DECISION: Let support agents perform customer refunds within a controlled authority model. FACT: Payment provider exposes full and partial refund APIs. FACT: Support role currently has read-only billing access.
contract.T: DECISION: Allow support agents to issue refunds up to $100 without owner involvement. DECISION: Require a reason for every support-issued refund. DECISION: Require owner involvement for refunds above $100. DECISION: Allow both full and partial refunds within the $100 support limit.
contract.S: FACT: No approval threshold or audit event exists today. DECISION: This slice covers authority limits, reason capture, refund type allowance, and owner escalation for larger refunds. UNKNOWN: Audit-event design is not yet specified, though the gap is known.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify support can create full or partial refunds up to $100 only when a reason is supplied. DECISION: Verify refunds above $100 cannot complete without owner involvement. DECISION: Verify existing read-only billing access is expanded only for the approved refund actions.
contract.X: DECISION: Stop after the reversible authority boundary, escalation rule, and verification expectations are defined. UNKNOWN: Detailed audit-event implementation remains outside this contract slice.
contract.P: DECISION: Use the $100 support limit with mandatory reason and owner escalation above that as the reversible default. DECISION: Revisit if finance policy or audit requirements change.
